transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (Suncrest CTO), Maya (Suncrest ML), Rita (Suncrest Infra)

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood inference, and with me is priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Daniel: good thanks, lena, excited to see the model catalog. we chatted briefly over email — main ask today is understanding open model options and how they'd run in our dedicated or private setup.
[00:12] Maya: yep, and mostly focused on latency / cost tradeoffs and whether quantized variants will preserve answer quality for our triage assistant.
[00:18] Rita: and from infra i'll be listening for VPC/on-prem constraints, network egress, and KMS compatibility.
[00:24] Priya (Redwood SE): great — quick agenda: we will demo the model catalog UI in the console, show curated open models, walk the benchmark table (throughput, median & p99 latency, token cost), and then show the compatibility matrix for quantization and hardware (a100, h100, intel xpu-ish references). we'll also cover routing/fallback policies and how to pin model versions.
[00:40] Lena: sounds good — quick qual question, maya — what does your request mix look like? short prompts, or longer context? and p99 latency SLO target?
[00:48] Maya: typically 80% short prompts — like 30-60 tokens — and 20% longer summaries maybe up to 512 tokens. p99 target ideally under 700 ms for interactive use, but we'll take input on cost tradeoffs.
[00:59] Priya: that's very helpful. on the demo i'll filter models that perform well for short prompt centric workloads and show batching settings that keep average latency low while lowering token cost.

Demo starts:
[01:15] Priya: ok i'm sharing screen — this is the model catalog. top left we have filters: license (open vs commercial), architecture family (llama, mosaic, llama2, bloom variants), quantization support, recommended use cases.
[01:30] Priya: klicking into an open model, you'll see a performance card: median latency, p95, p99, throughput (tokens/sec) on our hosted infra, and a separate column for dedicated and private profiles. note these numbers are measured with our internal harness and vary by sequence length and batching policy.
[01:45] Daniel: quick question — are those benchmarks for FP16 or int8 quantized runs?
[01:49] Priya: good point — we show separate rows: FP16, int8, and int4 (where available). and there's a compatibility column that indicates if we validated the quantized weights on a given hardware + runtime. sometimes int4 numbers are best-effort and flagged as experimental.
[02:05] Maya: do you have quality regression numbers when quantizing — like eval differences on our summarization set?
[02:10] Priya: we provide delta-bleu / delta-rouge style snapshots for common benchmarks and a small evaluation harness customers can run. for larger production checks we recommend running your prompt suite. we can help with that as part of the pilot.
[02:22] Rita: on private deployment — how does the catalog tie to the private control plane? if we pick an open model variant do we need to bring our own weights or can you pull them?
[02:30] Priya: for private on-prem, you can either provide the model artifacts, or permit redwood to fetch from a public registry into your private registry. we support S3-compatible pulls and can integrate with your artifact repo. all pulls respect your KMS and we never store plaintext keys.
[02:42] Lena: also to note, for certified customers we offer an assisted onboarding where we do a transfer into your VPC with your KMS keys.

Benchmarks & compatibility discussion:
[03:00] Priya: here's an example compatibility matrix row — model name: open-llama-13b-int8, supports kv-cache = yes, tokenizer = sentencepiece (note differences), validated on a100 fp16 and h100 int8 paths. network footprint: cold-start weights ~26GB compressed; warm KV cache sizing depends on max sequence.
[03:20] Maya: can you explain the tokenizer caveat? we have a custom tokenizer pipeline that includes de-dup token merging — will that break?
[03:27] Priya: usually tokenizer differences show up as tokenization drift and subtle quality differences — we can run your tokenizer preprocessor in our harness. if you have a forked sentencepiece model we can plug it in.
[03:38] Daniel: and batching — in dedicated mode how much control do we get? we can't have library-level batching that spikes p99 beyond our SLO.
[03:45] Priya: you get full policy control — concurrent procs limit, max batch size, and latency-aware batching that will flush after a latency budget. you can pick a latency SLO and redwood will tune batching heuristics; we expose metrics in the console so you can see p50/p95/p99 per-route.
[03:59] Rita: what about pre-warming and cache persistence across restarts?
[04:03] Priya: we support persistent KV cache snapshots, and options to keep a warm pool. for critical routes we recommend reserving instances or using dedicated reserved capacity so you don't hit cold starts.

Natural speech + small transcription noise:
[04:20] Daniel: (laughs) cool, okay so like — if we pick an open model that looks good in int8, we could run it in the dedicated pool and if traffic spikes it falls back to a cheaper hosted variant?
[04:30] Lena: yes — exactly. routing policies let you set tier fallbacks by region or cost threshold. and you can pin a route to a specific model version for safety.
[04:38] Maya: i noticed in the catalog there's a "quality delta" column — what's the baseline?
[04:42] Priya: baseline is usually the FP16 reference run on the full model. the delta is measured on a mix of eval suites — summarization, instruction-following, and a few internal tasks. for enterprise customers we can plug in your evals and show per-prompt deltas.

Security & compliance:
[05:05] Rita: on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys for both hosted and private? FIPS compliance?
[05:10] Lena: yes, we support KMS integrations and bring-your-own-key for private deployments; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS. we also have SOC 2 in scope and can share our audit artifacts in the security docs. FIPS modules depend on the underlying cloud/hardware but we can discuss options with your compliance team.
[05:25] Daniel: any red flags around PHI/PII? we need to ensure data residency and audit logging.
[05:30] Priya: we have audit logs per-request, retention controls, and region pinning for data locality. for PHI we often recommend private deployment with VPC peering or on-prem to minimize egress. we also capture request-level metadata for troubleshooting, and you can elect to disable retention for certain routes.

Customer concerns & tradeoffs:
[05:55] Maya: i'm worried about quantization regressions for long-format summarization — the int8 helps cost but if quality drops it's not worth it.
[06:01] Priya: totally — the pragmatic path is to run parallel A/B with FP16 for a percentage of traffic and track eval metrics; redwood console supports rollout policies and automatic rollback if quality dips beyond thresholds.
[06:13] Daniel: cost modeling — do you give per-token cost estimates by model + quantization?
[06:18] Priya: yes the console shows token unit-costs per model/variant and projected monthly cost based on your traffic profile — we can import your request distribution spreadsheet and produce a cost estimate (we'll do that after the call).

Recap + next steps:
[06:40] Lena: to recap — we'll send the full model catalog PDF, the compatibility matrix, and a benchmark sheet. priya will run a compatibility check for the top 3 open models you flagged and test your tokenizer and quantization path. we'll schedule a technical deep dive with rita and infra next tuesday to scope the pilot.
[06:58] Daniel: sounds good. can you also include sample configs for latency-aware batching and a sample rollout policy?
[07:03] Priya: yes — i'll attach example yaml snippets and a runbook for canarying models.
[07:07] Rita: please include network diagrams for VPC peering and on-prem agent.
[07:11] Lena: will do. any other questions?
[07:14] Maya: no, that's it for now — thanks, this was really useful.
[07:17] Daniel: thanks everyone.

Meeting ends.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hear of acronyms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cash), and speaker overlap in a couple places.
